PrimitiveIntegers.Aliases: i8 i16 i32 i64 i128 u8 u16 u32 u64 u128 are ordinary iN/uN spellings with those widths.
PrimitiveIntegers.Rule: No implicit integer promotion changes bit width.
usize and u64, isize and i64 have the same width on every target (x86_64, aarch64) and coerce to each other implicitly; pointers, slices and arrays of them stay distinct types.
@bitSizeOf(iN|uN) = N; standalone @sizeOf = ceil(N/8); packed fields occupy exactly N bits.

MlxTypeSystem.Bool: Other bit patterns are invalid bool values.

Conversions.Rule: A comptime integer or float may coerce when exactly representable or when the target conversion rule permits rounding for floats.
*T may coerce to *const T; const may never be implicitly removed.
*[N]T may coerce to [*]T and to [*]const T, *const [N]T to [*]const T: the address of the array's first element, its length dropped.

IntegerOperations.Builtin: Counts set bits in the declared width of an integer up to 64 bits.
Reads 64 bytes from a valid u8 pointer and returns bit i set exactly when pointer[i] equals the low eight bits of needle.

Builtin.name: @sqrt(value)
Builtin.result: the operand's float type; f64 for a float literal

FloatOperations.Builtin: The correctly rounded square root of an f32 or f64, one instruction (sqrtss/sqrtsd on x86_64, FSQRT on AArch64). A negative operand gives NaN, -0.0 gives -0.0; an integer operand is rejected.

Builtin.name: @floor(value) @ceil(value) @trunc(value)
Builtin.result: the operand's float type; f64 for a float literal

FloatOperations.Builtin: An f32 or f64 rounded to a whole number down, up or toward zero, exactly, one instruction (roundss/roundsd, SSE4.1, on x86_64; FRINTM, FRINTP, FRINTZ on AArch64). The sign of a zero result follows the operand (@ceil(-0.25) is -0.0); infinities and NaN come back as they are; an integer operand is rejected.

Slices.Field: The first word: the address of the first element.
The second word: how many elements.

Arithmetic.forms: p + n, p - n, p += n, p -= n
Arithmetic.operand: [*]T on the left, any integer on the right

Pointers.Arithmetic: Moves the address by n * @sizeOf(T) bytes, as &p[n] would. An integer on the left (n + p), any other operator, and single-item pointers (including *[N]T) are rejected.

CopySemantics.Rule: Values are copied by value. There are no implicit copy constructors, move constructors, or destructors.
Copying a pointer copies the address. Copying a slice copies its pointer and length, not referenced data.

MlxTypeSystem.EvaluationOrder: Subexpressions and function arguments evaluate left-to-right, except explicit short-circuit operators.

ShortCircuit.and: evaluate RHS only when LHS true
ShortCircuit.or: evaluate RHS only when LHS false
